sections.body_en:
1

I thank Hashem for having helped me complete the book 'Ḥafetzei Kodesh' within the 'Peninei Halakha' series, containing the laws of tzitzit, tefillin, mezuza, the Sefer Torah, the writing of STaM, the honour of the synagogue and its building, geniza and the reading of the Torah. The subjects in this book were printed in brief, together with further subjects, in Peninei Halakha parts 1 and 2, which were published more than thirty years ago, in 5753 and 5754. They were a rewriting of the halakha segments that were broadcast on the radio station 'Arutz Sheva'. Over time I began to write the 'Peninei Halakha' series as a systematic halakhic book unconnected to the halakha segment, in such a way that every subject would be clarified in full, with the intention that the laws printed in the first editions according to the 'halakha segment' would be upgraded and integrated into the systematic books. Most of the laws that were until now in Likkutim 1 are now included in this book. And from now on only the book Likkutim 2 will remain. By the kindness of God, with the completion of this book I have finished including all the subjects of the Shulḥan Arukh, part 'Oraḥ Ḥayim', within the 'Peninei Halakha' series.

2

The subjects this book deals with are the foundation of religious life, of realising the bond between a person and his Creator as an individual, as a family and as a community. Because of their great importance and holiness, and their great frequency in daily life, the laws, discussions and customs of the communities concerning them are many. As is my way in 'Peninei Halakha', I have tried to explain the laws from the general to the particular, down to the practical halakha, including the customs and rulings of the various communities in Israel. In addition, I have tried to convey the main contents of the mitzvot in their spiritual meanings.

In these laws there are subjects connected to scribes of STaM and makers of tefillin, and in them I did not go at length into all the details needed by professionals alone; rather I explained in depth and at length the halakhic foundations needed by every Jew within the fulfilment of the obligation of the mitzva of studying Torah and knowing it.

At times I went at length in the notes, in order to help learners grasp fundamental, long and complex issues in short and clear language, with the principle the Sages set (Pesaḥim 3b), "A person should always teach his student in a concise way", before my eyes. So that one who wishes to grasp the practical halakha together with the foundations of the reasoning and the reasons can make do with study without the notes. And one who wishes to go deeply into the issues should study the notes too, and he too will be able, in relatively short study, to grasp all the laws in depth.

3

As in all the books, I wrote and polished the laws again and again, dozens of times, until the final version printed in the book. In the recent books, in which the members of the Institute are partners in clarifying all the issues, I first write the laws, the main sources and the framework of the notes, noting the main lines of reasoning that need to be further examined or established, and noting the issues in which the weight of the poskim standing behind each view needs to be checked. After that I receive the summaries of the issues, answering the questions I raised, with suggestions for further clarifications needed to complete the subject. And again I examine and formulate the laws and the notes, and make the ruling precise, in discussion with the members of the Institute and receiving further suggestions for laws and ideas, mainly in the footnotes. In the last stage I go back and polish the wording again and again, and in the course of this I identify the issues that still need further examination, to which I return to study alone or with the help of the members of the Institute. Finally the members of the Institute carry out final proofreading, and I accept or reject their corrections and suggestions, and again proofread each chapter several times, and those working on the issue check that my last corrections improved matters and did not do the opposite.

4

In recent years the Institute has been growing in wisdom and in number, and my cooperation with the members of the Institute keeps deepening. The members of the Institute study the issues in depth, encompassing all the views of the Rishonim and Aḥaronim on the issue. Out of the close fellowship of study they examine the reasoning well and define the various views precisely, and thanks to this I am able in a relatively short time to grasp the various views and to know which way most of the poskim leaned in the various communities and in Israel as a whole, and on this basis to write the practical halakha in a richer and more precise way. All this in addition to the great help in proofreading and suggestions for the wording of the book, which raise the level of explanation and precision in the formulation of the laws, the reasoning and the ideas.

Precisely because the book deals with halakhic subjects that come up frequently, the commentaries and views on them are very many, and the challenge before the members of the Institute was greater: to encompass all the words of the Rishonim and Aḥaronim in their commentaries on the Gemara, on the Shulḥan Arukh and in the responsa of the poskim.

5

We have merited that our beit midrash in Har Bracha, which includes the yeshiva, the Institute and the settlement, contains Torah scholars from the various communities in Israel, and so the book comes out rich and precise in the customs of the various communities.

Since the laws in this book are daily ones, I was naturally asked over decades, by the residents of the settlement and the students of the yeshiva, many questions, and in the course of the practical answers the balanced weight of the ruling became clearer and clearer. I also learned what needs to be explained in a halakhic book addressed to the wider public, and in this the words of the Sages were fulfilled in me (Ta'anit 7a): "From my students more than from all of them."

6

It is a great privilege for me to thank the close partners in studying the issues and writing the book: Rav Maor Kayam shlit"a, head of the Har Bracha Institute, who for many years now has accompanied me throughout the study, and with his talent and diligence helps to examine the issues, rejoices in my explanations and novel insights and at the same time criticises them meticulously, and manages with a strong hand the teamwork of the members of the Institute, so that everything comes out properly examined. Likewise many thanks to the rabbis of the Har Bracha Institute, outstanding in their talent and wisdom, for their help in clarifying the issues, examining the views and the ideas, and in proofreading.

Rav Efrayim Shaḥor, who with the breadth of his study went deeply into important issues and also directed some of the clarifications made by the young rabbis. Rav Yair Weitz, who with his great diligence, even during his long service in the reserves, continued to go deeply into the issues and make them precise as though he were sitting in the beit midrash. Rav Uri Sharel, who with his sharpness makes the various views precise, analyses them and criticises every error. Rav David Pomerantz, who with wisdom and system arranges the views. Rav Noam Bernfeld, who in addition to clarifying the issues diligently, responsibly manages the uploading of the summaries of the Institute's rabbis to the internet. Rav Elad Bernstein, who with expertise and joy uncovers treasures in the issues. My son-in-law Rav Avishai Lax, who joined in the middle of this book, and with an overall and responsible view examines the issues well down to the halakha. And likewise Rav Yonadav Zar, who with his great talent has for decades accompanied the writing of Peninei Halakha, both in clarifying the issues, especially those concerning mathematics and geometry, and in the wording and the linguistic precision. Likewise I thank my good and long-standing friend, the all-round scholar, Rav Ze'ev Sultanovitch shlit"a, who also studied many of the issues in the book with me.

7

The students of Yeshivat Har Bracha, together with a large group of the residents of the settlement, are partners in this book. In the framework of the shiurim in the yeshiva and the settlement I taught all the subjects in the book, and shared with the students the questions and explanations that newly arose. Their questions and suggestions made me wiser. Rabbis from among the members of the Institute too give regular shiurim in the settlement and in the yeshiva around the subjects we are dealing with, and in these shiurim too the issues are clarified and examined, and ideas and questions arise that reach me. So I merited that the subjects were clarified and examined again and again in several frameworks of study. The women's shiur too contributes its part, with questions and wise suggestions, and there was even an issue in which women reminded me of an important line of reasoning I had said about twenty years ago in the laws of geniza.

8

Offerings of thanks to my father and teacher, Rav Zalman Barukh Melamed shlit"a, head of Yeshivat Beit El, and to my mother and teacher, Rabbanit Shulamit, from whom come all the foundations of my Torah and my outlook. In these laws the tradition stands out more, and I hope that something of the atmosphere of holiness, awe and love that I absorbed from my father and teacher in the days of my childhood breathes between the pages of this book. Likewise, special thanks to Inbal, my dear wife, who together with devoted care for our large family and rabbinic and educational activity in the settlement, places in first place her devotion to magnifying the Torah and glorifying it, to my success in study and to creating comfortable conditions for writing the books for the benefit of the many. May it be His will that we merit to see all our sons and daughters, our sons-in-law and daughters-in-law, our grandsons and granddaughters, rising in Torah study and keeping the mitzvot, establishing good and glorious families, and increasing truth, kindness and peace for ever.

I further thank all those engaged in the holy work of building the yeshiva and printing the books: R. Yaakov Weinberger, director general of the yeshiva, who is also a full partner in all the ideas examined in the books. And likewise Yoni Buzaglo, who is responsible for printing and marketing the books, and who is also careful to take part in the shiurim. Likewise, thanks to all the other dear and devoted people who work for the spread of the Torah, thanks to whom the books go up onto the internet and the various apps for the benefit of the many.

May it be His will that Hashem give all those who help and assist in the work understanding and strength to succeed in their work, and may they merit to establish glorious families, and may God fulfil all the wishes of their hearts for good.

9

We are still standing in a hard war against our enemies, with many of the students and graduates of our yeshiva fighting at the front in the regular army and in the reserves. Nevertheless, when they return to the yeshiva they study with desire and enthusiasm, and even contribute their part to examining the issues in the book. May it be His will that the merit of Torah study stand for all Israel and for our holy soldiers to defeat our enemies and to establish the rebirth of Israel in its Land and its State.

 

Eliezer Melamed

Iyar 5786
